name: json-write
algorithm: Parse a 1 MB JSON document (tools/bench gen kind json, seed 2) once into each language's std tree type, then serialise the tree as compact JSON into an in-memory buffer reps times (README.md).

skip.c: no std JSON: C has no standard JSON writer; no library stands in
skip.rust: no std JSON: Rust std has none (serde_json is a crate); no crate stands in
skip.mk-wrap: the checksum already uses the wrapping operators; the writer has no arithmetic to wrap

no_counts: B24 does not apply: an idiomatic row compares libraries, each with its own algorithm; the checksum (the output's length summed over reps) checks that every writer wrote the same compact text up to member order
notes: Idiomatic standard library (plan/06-m6.md 4.1): Mk Value's Format (compact, escapes as RFC 8259 section 7 requires) into a Text through its Writer, cleared per rep; Go encoding/json Encoder with SetEscapeHTML(false) into a bytes.Buffer reset per rep (keys sorted, the trailing newline not counted); Zig std.json.Stringify.valueAlloc into an ArenaAllocator reset per rep, numbers kept as text (parse_numbers = false). The parse runs once and is outside what the reps measure, but inside the program's time. Bytes per second = output length x reps / median.
